title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Nasdaq rallied 1.1% Friday, clawing back some of Thursday's 5.5% plunge (worst day since the April 2025 tariff panic) that had pushed the index into correction territory, down ~14% from its Oct. 7 peak; S&P 500 +0.3%, Dow -0.5%, Nasdaq still -3.4% on the week.
Markets: Hardest-hit AI-buildout names rebounded Friday - AMD +11%, Intel +7.7%, CoreWeave +6.3% - after Thursday's SOX semiconductor index plunge of 12.3%, its worst since the pandemic.
Markets: 10-year Treasury yield ~4.87%, crude ~$90.48/bbl, gold ~$4,074/oz (-0.95%), bitcoin ~$75,789 as the week wound down.

Companies: Anthropic's planned $1.5T IPO is in doubt - WSJ reports major prospective investors are skeptical it can hit that valuation after this week's AI selloff, with one floating a cut closer to $1T; Anthropic had been eyeing a listing the week before Thanksgiving.
Companies: Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production next year as it pivots toward autonomous vehicles and robotics; shares rose 4.2% Friday but are still down more than 10% on the week.

Macro/Policy: Trump named Stephen Miller his new White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles, a move seen as signaling a more confrontational posture toward corporate America and Democrats after the midterms.
Macro/Policy: Next week's calendar: October CPI (Tue) and PPI (Fri) inflation reports, plus earnings from KKR, Constellation Energy, Cisco Systems, Applied Materials and Bending Spoons.
